central_topic: Budgeted selection of benchmark columns and prediction of unmeasured new-model scores from incomplete historical score matrices, using masked low-rank factors and predictive-variance reduction on MTEB and Open LLM Leaderboard data.
core_methods: Masked low-rank matrix factorization by alternating regularized least squares, with historical held-out-cell rank selection
Greedy covariance-trace predictive-variance reduction over available benchmark columns
Conditional ridge reconstruction of new-model latent factors from purchased scores
comparators: Random benchmark selection with the same low-rank predictor
Selected-benchmark ridge prediction and correlation-central representative selection with ridge prediction
Historical task means and purchased-score mean-offset transfer
Within-benchmark item reduction: the explicitly permitted tinyBenchmarks and metabench starter papers
Latent-skill performance prediction and cross-family observational scaling: the explicitly permitted Observational Scaling Laws and Sloth starter papers
benchmarks: MTEB embedding-task score matrix; embeddings-benchmark/results revision 6dabbcc68c28ea5f180ce7df79347b3ca9cc6383
Open LLM Leaderboard contents score matrix; revision 9c09a7cae43334062a82cb164f2ef255013dafa2; six Raw benchmark columns
result_driven_themes: Structured cross-task dependence: the retained method scores above its column-permuted control, which preserves marginal scores and missingness
Value of informed query selection relative to random-query low-rank prediction, with a positive recorded paired family-clustered gain interval
Evaluation under both model-held-out and heuristic-family-held-out splits, without claiming verified architecture transfer or universal family robustness
Improving recorded budget curves in two separately evaluated populations: embedding models and generative language models; not a jointly fitted cross-population transfer experiment

queries.rationale: The retained source fits masked alternating ridge factors and reconstructs unseen scores. Foundational collaborative-filtering literature supplies the matrix-completion neighborhood without a broad search for the prohibited benchmark-prediction paper; it does not imply missing-at-random guarantees.

Selection reduces aggregate target predictive variance through a regularized latent covariance update. Classical prediction-oriented experimental design is the relevant analogy, not generic optimization or a claim that the implementation exactly optimizes an unqueried-only risk.

This explicitly permitted starter establishes the item-budget reduction comparator. Distinguish fewer examples within a benchmark from purchasing whole benchmark columns; tinyBenchmarks was not an executed baseline here.
